text.p: A merger between AT&T Corp and SBC Communications Corp could lead to SBC Chairman Edward Whitacre being named chief executive and eventually chairman of the new entity, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
In a report about the possible merger also carried in the Los Angeles Times and the Washington Post, SBC was described as the largest provider of local telephone services in the United States.

In 1996, it posted net income of $2.1 billion on revenues of $13.90 billion. SBC only recently closed its $16.7 billion acquisition of Pacific Telesis, a former part of AT&T that emerged when the company was broken apart under court supervision in 1984.

In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said such a scenario would leave AT&T Chairman Robert Allen's handpicked successor, President John Walter, unable to fulfil the plan of his being appointed to those top posts.
"You can only end up with one chief," an unnamed industry executive who knows the three men told the Journal. "I can't imagine Whitacre agreeing to a deal unless he is CEO."

The Journal reported Tuesday that the two telecommunications companies were in the midst of merger talks in a deal valued at more than $50 billion, leading to wide speculation about management changes.

The CNBC financial cable TV channel reported Tuesday that a plan was under discussion in which Walter, who joined AT&T seven months ago, would become chief executive of the combined companies and Whitacre would become a non-executive chairman, with a strategic planning role.

The merger "would create a companmy with nearly $80 billion in annual revenue, 240,000 employes, 31 million local telephone lines in California, Texas and five other southwestern states and 90 million long-distance customers worldwide," the Post reported.
